_comment: Two-layer: 'US' rows are the federal layer and apply everywhere. A state row with the same program_key REPLACES the federal row (e.g. Florida caps its nonrecurring reimbursement at $1,000, below the $2,000 federal ceiling). eligibility_json gates a program: special_needs / military.

detail: A one-time reimbursement for reasonable and necessary adoption fees — court costs, attorney fees, and other adoption-related expenses. The federal ceiling is $2,000; each state sets its own rate up to that amount.

A recurring monthly payment for a child eligible for federal adoption assistance, administered by the state and generally lasting until the child reaches the age of majority. The amount is negotiated per child, so no dollar range is published nationally.
A child eligible for federal adoption assistance is entitled to both a monthly subsidy and Medicaid.
The Department of Defense reimburses up to $2,000 per child, or up to $5,000 per year, for adoption expenses incurred by military families.

Florida pays $5,000 annually, on a monthly basis, for the support and maintenance of the child until the 18th birthday — or another amount agreed in writing between the adoptive parents and the department. The monthly payment may not exceed the foster care maintenance payment the child would otherwise have received.
Florida reimburses up to $1,000 in nonrecurring expenses — attorney fees, court costs, birth certificate fees, travel, agency fees, and physical examination fees.
Children receiving a monthly subsidy are eligible for health care through Medicaid until age 18; some children remain eligible until age 21.
Children adopted from Florida care are eligible for free tuition at any Florida state university, community college, or vocational school, up until age 28.
